messages.content: How is the air quality in Los Angeles right now?

function.name: plant_biomass
function.description: Calculate the biomass of a plant species in a given area. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

species_name.description: The name of the plant species.

area.description: The area of the forest in square kilometers. This is a float type value.

message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to current air‑quality data. For the most up‑to‑date information you can check one of the following:

| Source | How to use |
|--------|------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and view the latest AQI and pollutant levels. |
| **World Air Quality Index (WAQI)** | Go to https://waqi.info/, search for “Los Angeles,” and see the live AQI, PM2.5, PM10, O₃, NO₂, SO₂, CO values. |
| **Local news or weather apps** | Many local news stations (e.g., ABC7, CBS Los Angeles) publish real‑time air‑quality alerts on their websites or mobile apps. |
| **Mobile apps** | Apps like AirVisual, Plume Labs: Air Report, or the EPA’s AirNow app provide push notifications for AQI changes. |

If you need a quick snapshot, you can also use a voice assistant (Google Assistant, Siri, Alexa) and ask, “What’s the air quality in Los Angeles right now?” They pull data from the same public APIs.
